Hi Sofia / Liam 


Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery:

Recap (what we heard)
- Goal: Replace current rule-based translations and localized completions pipeline with a single inference path that maintains locale-specific quality for key EU and APAC markets while reducing per-token cost.
- Priority locales: French (FR), German (DE), Spanish (ES) for EU; Japanese (JP), Korean (KR) for APAC.
- Key success criteria: parity with current baseline on critical flows (product descriptions, customer support canned responses) and no regression >5% on human-rated quality per locale.

Recommended approach (short version)
1) Run a tied A/B eval using our RW-13B-Intl (quantized) as primary, with RW-7B-q as a low-cost fallback for tail queries.
2) Use localized prompt sets (we've attached prompt_set_v1.jsonl) and a per-locale evaluation harness (sample metrics: human-quality score, intent accuracy, fluency).
3) Two-phase PoC: smoke tests on a 1k-sample per locale, then a 10k-per-locale benchmark if smoke passes.

Attachments/Links:
- prompt_set_v1.jsonl (localized prompts for FR/DE/ES/JP/KR)
- multilingual_eval_plan.pdf (proposed schedule + metrics)
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-globex-multilingual

Questions for you (quick)
- Can you confirm the top 3 locales to start with? (we recommended FR/DE/ES + JP/KR but can stage)
- Do you have a set of representative queries we can use (200/sample locale ideal)? If there are PII concerns, we can provide an anonymized upload flow.

Next steps (proposal)
- You confirm locales + share a small sample (200 queries/locale) -> we run a 48-72h smoke test.
- Rafael/Dev and I run a technical deep-dive to align on latency targets, prefix caching, and quantization profiles (30-45m).
- If smoke looks good, expand to full 10k-per-locale eval and provide a regression report + tuned config.

I'll schedule the technical deep-dive (Rafael & Dev) for next week - proposed times on my calendar invite.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole

Adding some tech detail that will help Sofia's questions and make the PoC smooth.

Evaluation metrics we propose (high level):
- Human quality score: 5-point Likert on correctness/fluency/localization (3 raters/utterance). Target: no regression >5% vs baseline.
- Intent accuracy: automated classifier over labeled test set.
- Fluency / morphological checks: language-specific QA rules (e.g., unicode normalization, diacritics checks for FR/DE).
- Latency: p50/p95 server-side for 512-token completions; target p50 <300ms, p95 <700ms for primary config.
- Cost: tokens-per-response and cost delta vs current baseline.

Model recommendations / config:
- Primary: RW-13B-Intl (quantized int8) - good balance of quality across EU languages; we have tuned tokenizer merges for FR/DE/ES.
- Fallback: RW-7B-q for tails and burst capacity (lower cost).
- For JP/KR we may test an RW-13B-UTF variant (better multilingual tokenizer coverage).
- Enable prefix KV caching for repeated product-description prefixes to reduce latency during batch inference.
- Suggested batching: target dynamic batch sizes up to 8 for throughput, but run initial smoke with batch=1 to validate latency.

Data / sample needs:
- 200 anonymized queries per locale (CSV with columns: id, locale, prompt, expected_label/context).
- 50 gold-standard human references per locale for human scoring phase.

I've attached a quick template for results: multilingual_eval_results_template.csv and put a draft eval checklist in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-globex-multilingual

I'll join the tech deep-dive. Marissa - I recommend we allocate ~45 mins so we can walk through prompt examples and quantization tradeoffs.

--
